raw: 24.1 Defining the Gray Zone: Between Peace and War[^109][^110]
teaching_note: Gray-zone analysis concerns ambiguous competition often described as below overt-conflict thresholds; hybrid describes combinations of means and is not confined to that space, while irregular concerns a different mode of contestation. These terms vary by author and date: compare the cited accounts rather than announce one universal taxonomy. An analytic label is not a jurisdiction-specific legal finding that armed conflict does or does not exist [@ageint109; @ageint110].
title: Defining the Gray Zone: Between Peace and War

raw: 24.2 Gray Zone Tactics: Competition, Crisis, and Conflict[^111]
teaching_note: Use an indicator matrix with distinct columns for observable event, provenance/date, ordinary alternatives, inferred coordination, proposed sponsor, legal/policy threshold and missing evidence. Similar timing or cumulative disruption may merit a hypothesis but does not collapse those columns into attribution; an unresolved cell is not a zero or evidence of deniability. Classroom analysis does not select escalation or countermeasures [@ageint111].
title: Gray Zone Tactics: Competition, Crisis, and Conflict

raw: 24.3 Chinese Gray Zone: South China Sea and Taiwan Straits
teaching_note: Keep the geography and political context identifiable, but do not infer event-specific facts, maritime legal status or state direction from this heading. Broad CISA/NATO guidance is not case evidence for the South China Sea or Taiwan Strait; a comparison needs dated conduct records, source perspective, location uncertainty and the applicable legal question. Leave those historical cells unsupported until suitable records are supplied.
title: Chinese Gray Zone: South China Sea and Taiwan Straits

raw: 24.4 Russian Hybrid Warfare: Ukraine, Baltic States, Information Domain[^111]
teaching_note: Do not flatten different countries, periods and forms of conflict into one timeless below-war category. Attribute the professional article's analysis to its author and distinguish an observed incident from a claim about Russia's sponsorship or strategic purpose. Events in an armed conflict and ambiguous peacetime interference require separate factual and legal treatment [@ageint111].
title: Russian Hybrid Warfare: Ukraine, Baltic States, Information Domain

raw: 24.5 Anonymous No More: Countering Gray Zone Threats (MIPB 2025)[^111]
teaching_note: Completed offline case: B1 is a synthetic border-office delay log, B2 a weather closure notice, B3 a service-maintenance ticket, and B4 a repost attributing all delays to coercion but citing B1 only. The filled matrix confirms delay (B1), supplies independent benign mechanisms (B2/B3), and leaves coordination, sponsor and legal threshold unknown; B4 adds an interpretation, not an independent event source. Withheld B5 corrects B1's times to match scheduled maintenance, so lower the campaign hypothesis and correct the chronology; residual inconvenience does not establish intent. Stop at an attribution hold and a bounded service explanation, not tasking, escalation or public accusation (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]).
title: Anonymous No More: Countering Gray Zone Threats (MIPB 2025)

teaching_note: Treat the article's framework as a proposal for doctrine, not a universally adopted model or empirical law. Compare where its dimensions classify the same supplied incident differently from another author's account, and state why the difference is definitional rather than new evidence. No location in a conceptual matrix independently authorizes a policy or military response [@ageint110].
title: Full Spectrum Conflict Design (IWI 2025)
